prior_coverage:
No prior sweep of this family. A grep on 28.9 of docs/, research/ (all of it), logs/, MISSION.md and products/ for arrangeme, sheet music, musicnotes, mymusicsheet, score exchange, smp press, musescore, notation, lilypond, musicxml and IMSLP found 0 venue hits; the only matches were unrelated uses of 'arrangement'. The repo has no notation tooling either: a grep for music21, lilypond, musicxml and verovio in products/, src/ and scripts/ finds only node_modules MIME tables.

Nearest precedents that apply:
- Adobe was killed for having no contributor upload API, with login and CAPTCHA left to the user (docs/REJECTED.md:1006-1010).
- Signed-in web form per item: docs/REJECTED.md:1169 and 1172.
- CGTrader: no publishing API in any public code, so web-UI only (research/colony-sweep/groups/licensing-ip.md:166).
- 'Platform search ranks on prior success' (docs/REJECTED.md:1105-1121, law stated at :1117).
- 'Never sell what is already free' (docs/REJECTED.md:1240).
- The AI-music rejection (groups/licensing-ip.md:176) covers streamed audio, not notation.
- PayPal receiving works in Israel, with 18% VAT on fees since 6.7.2026 (docs/INCOME_PLAN.he.md:95).

New evidence this session (github grade), which changes the Adobe comparison for ArrangeMe only. Birdywen/genspark-agent, skills/reverse-engineering/arrangeme/, committed 22.2.2026, is a third-party Python SDK and batch uploader that drives ArrangeMe's private web endpoints over HTTP:
- A 4-step upload wizard, with PDFs pushed to S3 through unauthenticated Cognito.
- Publish and unpublish calls, plus the site's own /title/bulk/*.action endpoints.
- A CSV manifest for batch upload.
- Its stats lines read 'Stats: 8522 titles' and 'Stats: 6362 records, 2022-02-27 to present' on one account.
- Authentication is only a JSESSIONID cookie 'set by browser login'. The SDK has no login routine, so CAPTCHA, session lifetime and the terms of use on automated access are all unread.
- The repo also commits a third party's live session cookie. It must never be used.

Every other seed venue shows no bulk or API channel in public code, so each is killed on the Adobe precedent as the brief instructs. SMP Press is not a separate channel: the snippet says it is 'now part of Hal Leonard's ArrangeMe program'. MyMusicSheet has rebranded to mymusic5 (snippet). One venue was added: PaidTabs.

Egress: arrangeme.com and blog.arrangeme.com both returned EGRESS_BLOCKED to WebFetch.

candidates.venue: ArrangeMe (Hal Leonard; distributes to Sheet Music Direct, Sheet Music Plus and partners; SMP Press merged in)
candidates.what_we_would_list:
Notation only, under the Mehudak arranger name, with machine assistance declared in every description (the upload form's howModifiedDesc free-text field and the title description):
(a) Copyrighted-song lead sheets and level-graded instrumental parts: C, Bb, Eb and F transpositions, with range, key and difficulty machine-checked, sold under ArrangeMe's own licence at 10%. Only for songs where a verified melody source exists, because the colony cannot machine-check a transcribed copyrighted melody against the original.
(b) Public-domain melodies from verified MusicXML corpora, arranged for specific instrument × level cells. Only for cells where a runner has measured that no free equivalent exists on MuseScore or IMSLP (REJECTED.md:1240).
No audio, and no un-checked 'AI arrangements' of pop songs.
candidates.existing_product: None. The repo has no notation pipeline (0 hits for music21, lilypond, musicxml or verovio outside node_modules).
candidates.listings_per_owner_step: One account unlocks an unbounded catalogue: one third-party account holds 8,522 titles (github: Birdywen SDK stats). Each title goes to Sheet Music Direct and Sheet Music Plus and other Hal Leonard retail partners (snippet), so one owner step opens at least 2 storefronts.
candidates.prior_verdict: None. 0 repo hits for ArrangeMe (grep 28.9). The nearest kill shape is Adobe, docs/REJECTED.md:1006-1010: no upload API, and portal login plus CAPTCHA controlled by the user.
candidates.reopen_basis: Not a reopen. What is new against the Adobe precedent (github grade): Birdywen/genspark-agent skills/reverse-engineering/arrangeme (commit f185446, 22.2.2026) scripts the whole listing flow over HTTP. POST /sell/{publicdomain|original|copyrighted}/sheet/upload, then /details, /arrangement and /genres; GET /title/publish/{sellerTitleId}; PDF to S3 bucket 'arrangeme-uploads' via unauthenticated Cognito. batch_upload.py reads a CSV manifest with a 2 s delay between titles. A machine channel therefore exists; what is unknown is whether a machine can obtain and renew the session cookie.

gate_zero_cost.evidence:
Snippets:
- SMP Press (now ArrangeMe) 'is free to join'.
- The standard seller earns 50% of the Net Sale Price for original and public-domain titles and 10% for copyrighted arrangements, with no fee named.
- ArrangeMe PRO is optional, at 'less than $7 a month' (~$80/yr), for 52%/12%, and is not needed.
- 'Expanded Distribution for All Accounts' (blog title) suggests distribution is not gated on PRO.
The terms page itself has not been rendered.

gate_israel_payout_no_camera.evidence: No evidence found on ArrangeMe's payout method, country list or identity check. Two searches returned nothing on it, and arrangeme.com is egress-blocked. One snippet says subscription commissions are paid quarterly, about 30 days after the quarter ends, 'to your selected payment option' (unnamed). Hal Leonard is a US payer, so a W-8BEN is a likely one-time owner step (inference). Whether a camera step exists is unknown.

gate_programmatic_listing.evidence:
No documented API. The Birdywen SDK (github) demonstrates CSV-driven batch upload, publish, and the site's own bulk-edit endpoints (/title/bulk/selectAll.action, saveArrangementGroups, saveDifficultyLevels, with publish=true) on an 8,522-title account.
API_REFERENCE.md says: 'HttpOnly session cookie (set by browser login)', 'Closing browser does NOT invalidate session', 'Sign Out DOES invalidate session', and a session has expired when the API returns HTML. The SDK has no login method.
Three things are unread: whether login carries a CAPTCHA, how long a session lives, and whether the terms forbid automated access. If a human browser login is needed per session, this becomes the recurring-owner-work shape of REJECTED.md:1169/1172 and FAILs. If the colony can log in with the brand credentials, it PASSes. Also, 'Processing may take hours (backend review, PDF validation, distribution to sales channels)'.

gate_ai_allowed_honest.evidence:
No ArrangeMe AI policy was found (snippet search returned none; terms unrendered).
The upload form has 'howModified (select: Change in arrangement/difficulty/style/Other)' and a free-text 'howModifiedDesc' (github). That is a place to state machine assistance, but it is not an AI field.
Honest-value risk (inference): ArrangeMe licenses the right to arrange a copyrighted song, not a reference melody (grade none). A melody the colony transcribed cannot be machine-verified, so lane (a) needs a verified source per song or it becomes the slop the mission forbids. Lane (b) passes REJECTED.md:1240 only in cells measured to have no free equivalent.

gate_buyer_supply.evidence:
Buyers reach a non-famous bulk catalogue here:
- github: the SDK's stats lines read 'Stats: 6362 records, 2022-02-27 to present' and 'Stats: 8522 titles' for one account. That is about 132 sales records a month over roughly 48 months, with SDK defaults of Piano Solo, $5.99 and type 'publicdomain'.
- snippet: titles are published 'to trusted online sellers including Sheet Music Plus and Sheet Music Direct'.
No retailer traffic numbers were seen.

candidates.discovery_needs_prior_sale: UNKNOWN. The search ranking of Sheet Music Direct and Sheet Music Plus has not been seen. Soft counter-evidence (github): the 8,522-title bulk account above logged 6,362 sales records in about 48 months, so buyers do find a mass catalogue with no known audience. Whether sales concentrate on titles that have already sold is unmeasured. The long-tail-cell hypothesis (song × instrument × level with few competitors) is unmeasured: a runner should render one Sheet Music Direct search results page for one song and count arrangements per instrument and level.
candidates.owner_step:
One-time only:
1. Open an ArrangeMe (Hal Leonard) seller account under the Mehudak brand.
2. Set the payout method (method UNKNOWN).
3. Submit the US tax form (W-8BEN, inference).
4. Hand the colony the login credentials, so it can log itself in.
Whether a pen-name arranger can be paid under the owner's legal name is UNKNOWN. If login is CAPTCHA-gated, step 4 becomes recurring and the venue fails.
candidates.estimate_basis:
INFERENCE.
Base rate (github): one bulk account logged 6,362 sales records from 2022-02-27 to 22.2.2026 (~48 months), ending with 8,522 titles. That is at least 0.0155 sales per title per month. It is a floor, because the catalogue grew during the window, and 'records' may include low-value subscription lines.
Commission (snippet): 50% of net sale price for public-domain or original titles, 10% for copyrighted. SDK default price is $5.99, and the minimum for Easy Piano is $4.99 (github).
Assumptions: 1,000-2,000 honest titles live at month 12, at ₪3.6 per dollar.
- Copyrighted only: 1,000 × 0.0155 × ~$0.55 ≈ ₪30 a month.
- Public domain or original: 2,000 × 0.0155 × ~$3 ≈ ₪335 a month.
High end rounded to ₪350. Low end ₪0: any of three unknown gates (login and session, terms on automation, AI policy) or the honest-value filter can zero it.
Popular copyrighted songs probably sell more per title, but there is no base rate for that, so it is excluded.
candidates.time_to_first_sale: Inference: at the github base rate of about 1 sale per 65 titles per month, 100 live titles would give about 1.5 sales a month. That puts a first sale about 1-2 months after the first 100 titles clear processing ('may take hours'), and the clock starts only after the owner step and the three renderable tests. Payout timing is UNKNOWN; subscription commissions are paid quarterly (snippet).
